item.title: “Can't qualify as ‘electrifying',” Aakash Chopra trolls Shehbaz Sharif for congratulating Pakistan on beating Australia's B side
item.description: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif commended the national cricket team’s performance in the first T20I against Australia in Lahore on Thursday (January 29). The Men in Green defeated the visitors by 22 runs at the Gaddafi Stadium to gain a 1-0 lead in the three-match series. A day after the game, Sharif took to X and congratulated Pakistan on beating the Australian side missing quite a few of their first-choice T20I stars. item.title: PAK v AUS 2026: WATCH – Pakistani TV umpire makes hilarious gaffe while reviewing Babar Azam’s DRS call in 1st T20I
item.description: The first T20I between Pakistan and Australia in Lahore on Thursday (January 29) produced a comical moment, involving TV umpire Nasir Hussain. The match official was subjected to social media trolling after he made serious goof-ups while reviewing a DRS call, taken by the visiting team against Babar Azam. item.title: After Iceland, Uganda declare readiness for T20 World Cup 2026 if Pakistan pull out of global showpiece
item.description: Uncertainty remains over Pakistan’s participation in the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026, slated to be held in India and Sri Lanka from February 7 to March 8. Ever since Bangladesh’s removal from the tournament for refusing to travel to India citing security concerns, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has indicated that they are considering several options and a final decision on whether they take part in the marquee event will be made by their government. item.description: Australia spinner Adam Zampa delivered a stunning bowling spell in the first T20I against Pakistan in Lahore on Thursday (January 30), but it wasn’t enough to ensure victory for his team. Saim Ayub, Salman Ali Agha, Babar Azam and Usman Khan were his victims as Zampa returned with the figures of 4/24 in his four overs at the Gaddafi Stadium. item.title: IND v NZ 2026: “I see a shadow of Rohit Sharma,” Irfan Pathan appreciates Suryakumar Yadav’s leadership skills
item.description: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has commended Suryakumar Yadav’s leadership, saying the latter has not received the recognition he deserves despite delivering impressive outcomes as captain of the Indian T20I team. item.description: Legendary India cricketer Yuvraj Singh has mentored several young players in recent years, including Shubman Gill and Abhishek Sharma. item.title: IND v NZ 2026: “Our job is to keep him in a good…,” India batting coach on Sanju Samson’s struggles in New Zealand T20Is
item.description: Sanju Samson has struggled with the bat in the ongoing five-T20I series against New Zealand. His early dismissals to fast bowlers in the first three games, followed by his dismissal to a spinner after getting set, are concerning for India as they gear up to defend the T20 World Cup title at home. Despite producing paltry scores of 10, 6, 0, and 24, Samson has received backing from the Indian team management ahead of the series finale. item.description: India opener Abhishek Sharma might be making mockery of the bowlers around the world, but New Zealand pacer has a simple game plan to combat the southpaw -- keep him under pressure with relentless accuracy. item.title: “It's going to be tough in near future”: Temba Bavuma warns Gautam Gambhir of challenging period ahead as Test coach
item.description: While India’s white-ball side has been performing exceptionally well under head coach Gautam Gambhir, producing trophies and strong win-loss records, that success has not translated to the traditional format. With Gambhir at the helm, India have won seven, lost 10 and drew two of their 19 Tests so far, which includes a couple of clean sweeps against New Zealand (0-3) and South Africa (0-2) at home. item.description: England white-ball skipper Harry Brook has admitted that he was accompanied by his teammates when he was struck by a nightclub bouncer in New Zealand, contradicting his earlier explanation of the incident.
